$comment: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the simsys metric catalogue. Machine-readable
because three independent implementations of a supposedly identical
contract will drift, and prose cannot be executed.
JSON rather than YAML, and this is forced rather than stylistic: the CI
requirements are hash-pinned and carry no PyYAML, so a YAML-reading test
passes on a dev box and fails in CI. JSON parses dependency-free in all
three lanes. JSON has no comments, so rationale lives in `$comment` and
`notes` string fields.
WHAT READS THIS:
tests/test_metrics_contract.py          (python lane, live registry)
node/tests/contract-conformance.test.ts (node lane, live registry)
go/contract_conformance_test.go         (go lane, live registry)
tests/test_contract_cross_language_guard.py  (pytest lane -- the only
lane in the repo's required-checks list, so cross-language
invariants that must BLOCK a merge live there)
HOW TO CHANGE A METRIC: edit this file first, then the three lanes. The
conformance tests read the expected values from here, so an
implementation-only change goes red. That is the point.
notes_on_required_label: `service` is mandatory on every metric and is the join key with
{service="x"} | json in Loki. Both packages trim it, so a padded
spelling cannot become a second identity.
One service identity per process (Python, Node) or per Registry (Go).
A consumer needing two identities must run two processes.

status_class.notes: Status codes are collapsed to a class to bound cardinality. Out-of-range, non-numeric and negative inputs all fall to 5xx in every lane.

job_outcome.notes: Closed set of exactly two. Deliberately no timeout/cancelled/panic -- a wider set is a cardinality decision, not a convenience.

http_method.notes: RFC 9110 methods plus PATCH, with OTHER as the overflow. An allowlist rather than passthrough: arbitrary methods once created unbounded series.

memory_type_core.notes: The ONLY memory type every runtime emits. A cross-runtime dashboard panel must filter type="rss" or it double-counts on Node, where heapUsed is a subset of heapTotal is a subset of rss.

http_request_duration_seconds.notes: The 15/30/60 tail was added 2026-08-05. Before it the schedule stopped at 10.0, so every slower request fell into +Inf and histogram_quantile could never return more than 10 -- p95 was pinned at exactly 10.00 for any service with a real tail, and a 15s alert threshold was structurally unfirable. Buckets are baked in at instrumentation time, so a service only gets this after it upgrades and redeploys.

job_duration_seconds.notes: Was unpinned by any test in all three lanes until this contract existed -- a second instance of the gap that caused the HTTP ceiling bug, found while writing this file.

tiers.core: Guaranteed present in every runtime with the declared type and exact label set. A $service-templated dashboard may rely on these unconditionally.
tiers.extension: Runtime-specific. The `runtimes` array is authoritative -- a dashboard panel using one must tolerate its absence. Coverage is genuinely three-valued (some metrics are in two of three lanes), which is why `runtimes` is an explicit list rather than a boolean.

simsys_build_info.help: Service build information. Always equal to 1; read labels for actual data.

simsys_http_requests_total.help: Total HTTP requests handled, bucketed by status class.
simsys_http_requests_total.notes: `route` is a TEMPLATE, never a literal path. Literal paths are the classic unbounded-cardinality mistake.

simsys_process_memory_bytes.notes: Label NAMES match everywhere; the `type` VALUE set does not. Only rss is universal. Declared core because the metric and its labels are guaranteed -- the extra values are declared per runtime so a dashboard author can see the difference instead of discovering it.

simsys_scrape_errors_total.notes: Was registered but never incremented in Go until #50320 -- it read 0 forever while its own doc comment claimed otherwise.

simsys_runtime_gc_collections_total.notes: The ONLY metric in the catalogue whose label NAMES differ by runtime, which is what makes it look unintended rather than designed. Python reports CPython's three GC generations separately; Go reports a single runtime.MemStats.NumGC cycle count. A panel with `by (generation)` returns empty for Go services, and summing across lanes compares different units. Declared as it actually behaves -- NOT as it should -- so the conformance tests assert something true and stay green. Declaring the target here instead would ship a permanently-red check, and a check that is always red stops carrying information. Resolving #50345 means editing `current` to match `target` and flipping `status` to `specified`, in the same commit as the code change.

$comment: Every entry carrying status:divergent must appear here with a ticket.
This list is asserted against `expected_count` by the cross-language
guard, so adding a divergence is a deliberate edit to a NUMBER that a
reviewer sees -- not a line appearing in a list nobody reads. That is
what stops 'declare it divergent' becoming cheaper than fixing it.

behaviors.$comment: Semantics rather than shape -- the rules a JSON Schema cannot express. Same status/current/target vocabulary as metrics, one mechanism for both.

empty_operation_rejected.notes: Python emitted an operation="" series. Warns as of #50322; raises in the next major.

current.node: throws on falsy, warns on whitespace
trackQueue reports 0 silently; trackPool keeps previous values

poller_failure_policy.target: preserve last known value, leave series absent on first-tick failure, count on simsys_collector_errors_total
poller_failure_policy.notes: Three policies in one package, one of which contradicted its own README. Changing an emitted value, so it ships in its own release.

current.python: process-global, second install with a different service silently re-labels

service_identity.target: one identity per process (python, node) / per Registry (go); changing it is an error
